title: Low Angle Ring Illumination Stereomicroscopy for Drosophila Eye Imaging
author: Jukta Biswas
license_note: PMC full-text XML — Bio-protocol — CC-BY confirmed in article XML
materials: Adult flies (3 days old) of desired genotypes; we used GMR-GAL4/+; +/+, GMR-GAL4/+; UAS-HttQ138-mRFP/+ , and GMR-GAL4/+; UAS-FUS WT /+ lines for adult eye imaging in this study. Laboratory supplies
Glass slide (Blue Star microslide, 75 mm × 25 mm)

steps.title: Set up egg laying
steps.instruction: Place 5 male and 5 female parental flies in a vial with standard cornmeal food and allow them to lay eggs for 12 h.

steps.title: Culture F1 generation
steps.instruction: Transfer the parental flies to a new food vial and incubate the resulting F1 larvae and pupae at 24 °C with a 12 h light/12 h dark cycle until adult flies emerge.

steps.title: Clean adult eyes
steps.instruction: Collect 3‑day‑old adult F1 flies and place them in an empty clean vial for 10–20 min to allow removal of food debris from the eyes.

steps.title: Anesthetize flies
steps.instruction: Transfer 3–5 male/female flies to the etherizer and incubate until they stop moving (fully anaesthetized).

steps.title: Decapitate flies
steps.instruction: Immediately move the anaesthetized flies onto a glass slide and decapitate each head using a fine dissection needle or forceps (hold the thorax with one forceps and detach the head with another).

steps.title: Mount head for imaging
steps.instruction: Mount each head on the slide so that one eye is adhered with nail polish and the opposite eye faces upward and is visible for imaging.

substeps.instruction: Hold the mouthparts of the head with fine forceps and place the eye region on a small drop of transparent nail polish (Shade‑40).
Position the head on the glass slide with the nail‑polished eye adhering to the slide, leaving the other eye surface upward.
Use a fine needle or forceps to align the head, keeping the central part of the visible eye in focus.
Allow the nail polish to dry for 3–5 min; the sample is now ready for imaging.

steps.title: Prepare microscope stage
steps.instruction: Place a flat black plate on the stereomicroscope stage to avoid glare.

steps.title: Position slide on stage
steps.instruction: Center the slide with mounted eye samples on the stage.

steps.title: Install ring illuminator
steps.instruction: Place the ring illuminator at the stage, centered over the imaging area.

steps.title: Create illumination angle
steps.instruction: Add a 2–3 mm block beneath the ring illuminator to produce a 2–3° incline, preventing a central shadow on the eye.

steps.title: Set microscope magnification
steps.instruction: Set the stereomicroscope to its maximum magnification (8× on the SMZ800N).

steps.title: Open imaging software
steps.instruction: Launch NIS‑Element software for image acquisition.

steps.title: Center and focus sample
steps.instruction: Bring the mounted head to the center of the view and adjust focus to display the maximum portion of the eye surface.

steps.title: Focus on central eye region
steps.instruction: Concentrate on the central part of the eye, acknowledging that the curved surface prevents the entire eye from being in focus in a single image.

steps.title: Adjust exposure settings
steps.instruction: Set exposure time to 300 ms and gain to 1.0× in NIS‑Element.

steps.title: Perform white balance
steps.instruction: Run white balance using the same empty background; do not modify settings after this step.

steps.title: Capture high‑resolution image
steps.instruction: Capture the image with no binning to obtain a high‑resolution picture of the eye.

steps.title: Acquire sufficient eye images
steps.instruction: Capture images of at least 50 eyes per genotype, keeping all imaging parameters identical across genotypes and replicates.

steps.title: Score eye degeneration
steps.instruction: Quantify eye defects using a degeneration score that incorporates eye size, number and size of necrotic patches, pigmentation level, and ommatidial alignment/fusion.

steps.title: Calculate rescue effect
steps.instruction: Compute the degeneration score to assess whether the targeted molecule rescues or exacerbates neurodegeneration in the Drosophila compound eye.
